A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TAROT work and provide readable main texts, equations, figures, tables and appendices. Relocated sections and results can be matched reliably.

before.justification: V1 reports original influence-estimation, semantic-segmentation, motion-prediction and instruction-tuning experiments, including supplementary ablations.

after.justification: V2 retains these experiments and adds k-sensitivity results, TSDS comparisons and runtime measurements.

M1.justification: Projected-gradient whitening and normalization, fixed-size and OTM selection, and OT-potential weighting remain unchanged. Algorithms 1 and 2 retain the same procedures; the new k study evaluates an existing component.

E1.justification: Both versions use CIFAR-10, GTA5/Cityscapes, WOMD/Argoverse 2/nuPlan/nuScenes, and the same instruction-data mixture evaluated on MMLU and BBH. The added experiments use existing task and dataset coverage.

E2.justification: V2 adds TSDS to instruction-tuning comparisons in Appendix E, Table 6, and compares its runtime with TAROT and LESS. Existing TRAK, LESS, DsDm, random-selection and leaderboard comparators are retained.

E3.justification: Section 4.6 introduces an OTM sweep over k = 1, 5, 10, 15 and 20, evaluating target-set and test-set performance. Appendix G adds a timing protocol separating feature computation from selection. Table 6's contradictory caption does not reliably establish a changed OTM training budget.

E4.justification: The new k-sensitivity study tests alignment versus generalization, and the runtime analysis examines computational overhead. The whitening/normalization ablation is unchanged, moving from v1 Table 6 to v2 Table 2; existing qualitative and T-SNE analyses remain.

E5.justification: The 100-subset, 100-model LDS procedure is retained. V2 adds no repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty estimates for its new comparisons.

E6.justification: V2 adds TSDS MMLU/BBH scores of 65.2/63.1 for LLaMA and 73.9/66.2 for Qwen, k-sensitivity curves, and runtime results. Table 8 reports selection times of 59 seconds for TAROT-Fixed and 118 seconds for TAROT-OTM versus 10 hours for TSDS, alongside shared 32-hour feature computation. Original benchmark scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix G and Table 9 add asymptotic cost expressions, O(|D|N) for gradient computation and O(|D||Dtar|d) for selection. Existing influence, whitening and OT mathematics remain substantively unchanged; no new theorem or proof is supplied.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about WFD, OT-based targeted selection, data efficiency and broad applicability. New comparisons support these claims without redefining the central contributions.

C2.justification: V2 interprets increasing k as reducing target alignment while improving generalization up to approximately k = 10. It also discusses feature computation as the dominant, potentially amortizable cost. The existing limitation concerning overfitting to small or specific target datasets remains.

D1.justification: Table 8 newly identifies single-H100 timing measurements. Conversely, v2 removes v1's explicit segmentation settings of 50 training epochs, no augmentation and 920 × 460 image resizing; batch size 16 remains in Table 3. These omissions do not establish an actual procedural change. Code-access information is retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds Ermolov et al. on whitening and Liu et al.'s TSDS. Section 5 and Appendix E distinguish TAROT's whitened distances, greedy selection and stopping criterion from TSDS's continuous OT formulation. Earlier related work is retained, partly relocated.

P1.justification: Most existing prose remains intact, with local condensation and revised experimental questions. Related work moves after the experiments and partly into Appendix A; ablation and leaderboard discussions exchange main-text/appendix placement. V2 also adds an Impact Statement.

P2.justification: V2 reformats the document into the ICML layout and redistributes displays between the main text and appendices. It adds Figure 8 and Tables 6, 8 and 9, moves the existing ablation and leaderboard tables, and revises captions and legends. Most existing graphical data are retained.

improvement.justification: The new k-sensitivity study and direct TSDS accuracy/runtime comparisons modestly strengthen evidence for parameter choice and practical competitiveness. Original results are preserved. These benefits are tempered by omitted segmentation settings and Table 6's misleading caption, which describes OTM selection percentages as improvements and incorrectly says all rows use 5% of the data.
